reason: The fixed three-onset/four-period construction states all exposure probabilities, both potential-outcome paths, nonconstancy, eligible-period effect, three HT values, unbiased mean, variance, three null statistics, inclusive-tail p-values, grid calibration and all-level validity. Fin indices merely relabel calendar dates and onsets. The canonical assertion is the counterexample itself; the theorem establishes that assertion and only refutes the necessity reading it describes. The witness has one permanent onset, uniform assignment as sole randomness, all fixed current-exposure outcomes observed, and positive used denominators.

The first branch is the canonical overlap-period inverse-probability identity for arbitrary fixed real potential outcomes and any known finite schedule law, with current exposure built into the estimator. The second is inclusive-rank validity for every statistic under a nonempty uniform finite law and thus includes every fixed sharp-null path. The final clauses state both canonical raw-before-after biases, including the pointwise +2 identity under restored treatment. Arbitrary finite index types are equivalent to finite period labels, not a substantive restriction.

The K=k+2 populations, positive bounded fixed individual outcomes, individual effect, both pointwise allocation formulas, universal error bound, genuine full independent fair joint law, nonempty-arm probability, arbitrary-extension lower bound and limit, conditional mean, half-complete two-point law and variance limit, dominant share and six-cluster checks all match the canonical counterexample. The full independent parent, rather than only a dependent or conditioned design, supplies the required refutation witness. The canonical assertion is that this counterexample exists; the theorem establishes it.

The sequence theorem has precisely the uniformly bounded individual outcomes, common independent assignment or uniform complete quotas, one positive probability margin uniform in k, vanishing maximum population share and convergence-in-probability conclusion for every positive epsilon and every empty-arm extension. It states the squared-share equivalence, supplies the unchanged few-dozen-cluster bias possibility by a 24-cluster example, and includes an independent bounded-outcome counterexample when no dominance is dropped. No convergence of effects or assignment probabilities is required. The finite_lemmas are audit history, not additional clauses to demand.

The canonical statement and definitions_needed describe individual assignment with identical probabilities and assumptions (a)-(c), without imposing fixed treatment counts or conditional uniformity within counts. The theorem adds these substantive design assumptions: fixed counts almost surely plus actual marginals m/N, or a proper nonempty subset law uniform within each count. It includes complete randomization and independent common-p assignment conditional on nonempty arms. These are valid and nonvacuous subclasses; arbitrary equal-marginal dependent varying-count laws are excluded. The canonical note suggests subclasses but, by the task rule, cannot narrow the claim. The current docstring expressly discloses exactly this restriction.
